To ensure your websites are secured by WAF, you must add your domains to the WAF instance and set up protection policies. You can access the Security Overview page to view relevant records of requests and attacks, helping you stay updated on your business's security status.

<span id="b5c79cbc"></span>
## Background information

BytePlus WAF supports two types of instances, suitable for different business scenarios.


* WAF instance for CDN domains: Protects domains added to BytePlus CDN. Integrating WAF with CDN not only enhances website security but also improves business performance. which offers your users a faster and more secure experience.

* Cloud WAF Instance: Regardless of where your business is located, whether on BytePlus or elsewhere, you can easily configure website parameters and back\-to\-origin parameters to finalize the setup. You can add your domains to a Cloud WAF instance using CNAME records. Simply configure the parameters, allow the WAF's back\-to\-source IP addresses, and modify the DNS resolution records of the domain to complete the setup.


<span id="e6351036"></span>
## Prerequisites


* You have already created the proper WAF instance. For more details about creating an instance, see

   * [Creating a WAF instance to protect your domain names on CDN](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/waf/docs-system-management)

   * [Creating a Cloud WAF instance to protect your domain names](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/waf/Creating_a_Cloud_WAF_instance)

* The domain has not been added to the WAF instance yet.


<span id="74528271"></span>
## Precautions

When you add domains using CNAME records, WebSocket protocols are automatically supported and currently, there is no option to disable this feature.

<span id="85194f59"></span>
## Procedure

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

<span id="6882f364"></span>
## Step 1: Creating a WAF instance


1. Login to the Web Application Firewall Console.

2. In the top menu bar, select the region of your instance.

   * Asia Pacific (Johor): Cloud WAF instances can be created.

   * Edge (CDN): WAF instances for CDN domains can be created.

3. On the left\-side navigation pane, choose System management \> Instance management.

   * For more details about creating a cloud WAF instance, see [Creating a Cloud WAF instance to protect your domain names](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/waf/Creating_a_Cloud_WAF_instance).

   * For more details about creating a WAF instance for protecting CDN domains, see [Creating a WAF instance to protect your domain names on CDN](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/waf/docs-system-management).

      Once completed, the instance details will be available on the Instance management page.


<span id="d61d2635"></span>
## Step 2: Adding a domain to the WAF instance


1. On the left\-side navigation pane, select Website settings.

2. Add a domain to the WAF instance.

   * Add a domain to the cloud WAF instance.

      1. Configure website parameters and back\-to\-origin parameters. For more details, see [Adding a domain name to a Cloud WAF instance](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/waf/Allowing_back-to-origin_CIDR_blocks).

      2. Allow access from back\-to\-origin CIDR blocks of WAF. For more details, see [Adding the back-to-origin CIDR blocks to your allowlist](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/waf/Modifying_the_DNS_record).

      3. Check whether the forwarding takes effect. For more details, see [Verifying the configurations of your domain name ](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/waf/Verifying_website_settings).

      4. Modify the DNS record of the domain name to resolve the domain name to the CNAME provided by WAF. For more details, see [Modifying the DNS record of your domain name](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/waf/Adding_a_domain_to_a_cloud_WAF_instance).

   * Add domains accelerated by CDN service to the WAF instance. For more details, see [Adding a CDN domain name to a WAF instance](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/waf/37711).


<span id="73d93000"></span>
## Step 3: Configuring protection policies

After integrating the domain, the vulnerability protection policy is activated by default. It supports the defense against common public vulnerabilities and exposures (CVE) and [OWASP Top 10](https://owasp.org/www-project-top-ten/) vulnerabilities, including threats like SQL injection and Cross Site Scripting. You can also customize other protection policies to suit your specific security needs.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">Vulnerability protection policies are set to perform Block action by default to block all attack traffic, and any related attack activities will be recorded in the attack logs.</div>



1. On the left\-side navigation pane, select Protection policies.

2. Select different policy types to set up. For more details about protection policies, see [Introduction to WAF policies](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/waf/docs-introduction-to-custom-waf-rules).
